headline: Trump says Musk put Ukraine's Starlink back on.
summary: Ukraine's army runs its drones and missile warnings over Starlink, Elon Musk's satellite internet. A speed cap left the drones unable to keep up with Russian attacks. Musk says the US government controls that access; the White House says it ordered nothing. Trump now says Musk "put it back". Zelensky says it is not at full speed yet.

cover_question.q: Can he turn ours off too?

cover_answer: No. Ours doesn't come from his satellites.
table_question: Should one person hold the off switch for a whole country?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A country called Ukraine gets its internet from satellites, little machines up in space that a man named Elon Musk owns. For a while it got slow, like a hose with a kink in it, and nobody would say who put the kink there. Today the president said Musk fixed it. Your internet is fine, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: The kink in the hose is the whole story. Who did it stays with the grown-ups.
5-7.why_long: A child this age reasons from what is in front of them and takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them one: a hose with a kink in it, and a man who owns the satellites. The war and the drones stay off this card. Expect "why did it get slow?" Nobody will say, and that is the honest answer.

8-12.script: Ukraine's army uses Starlink, Musk's satellite internet, to fly its drones and to warn of Russian missiles. A speed cap slowed the drones. Musk said he didn't; the White House said it didn't. Two kids by a broken lamp, each pointing at the other, until Trump said Musk "put it back".
8-12.why: Cap, slow drones, two denials, one fix. The pointing is the part they know.
8-12.why_long: At this age a child is working out cause and effect and whether grown-ups own up when they break something, so the script runs one chain: a cap went on, the drones slowed, two people denied it, and the president says it is fixed. Two kids by a broken lamp is the mechanism they know. Expect "so who did it?" Nobody has admitted it.

13-17.script: Should one company get to throttle an army mid-war? Ukraine's drones run on Musk's Starlink, and a speed cap slowed them. Musk says the government controls access; Trump says Musk "put it back". Second: it came as Trump pressed Zelensky to stop hitting Russian refineries. What would link the two?
13-17.why: The off switch, then the timing. Let them say what they'd need to know.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a private network kept Ukraine's drones flying, and the president was pressing Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries. The script hands them both and asks what would link them; Kuhn's point is that arguing is practised on evidence. Expect "so did Trump do it?" Nobody has owned it.

5-7.q: Can he turn ours off too?
5-7.a: No. Ours doesn't come from his satellites. Ukraine borrows a special internet from space that his company owns.

8-12.q: Why does an army need internet?
8-12.a: Drones and missile warnings run on Starlink. Slow it, drones lag.
Nobody will say. Musk blames the government; it says it didn't.

13-17.q: Should one company hold an army's off switch?
13-17.a: Ukraine's army runs on a network it doesn't own. This week showed the cost.
The White House says no. Musk says the government holds the keys.
